name: CUET UG
approxCandidates: 15.69 lakh registered and 11.64 lakh appeared (CUET UG 2026)
eligibility: Passed or appearing in Class 12 (or equivalent). No age limit. Each university sets its own subject and percentage requirements.

notification.summary: CUET UG 2026 was held in CBT mode from 11 May 2026. Some papers were rescheduled to 31 May and 6–7 Jun because of Eid-ul-Azha. The result was declared on 23 Jun 2026: 15,68,867 candidates registered and 11,64,098 appeared. University admissions and counselling for 2026–27 are complete or wrapping up. The CUET UG 2027 notification is expected around Jan–Feb 2027 (the 2026 notification came out on 3 Jan 2026). Dates come from news reports via web search; cuet.nta.nic.in could not be reached from the research sandbox.
notification.source: https://cuet.nta.nic.in (official). Result figures from the NTA press release as reported by IANS (ianslive.in, 23 Jun 2026) and ETV Bharat.

pattern.notes: Since 2025, every CUET UG test has 50 compulsory questions in 60 minutes, scored +5 / −1. Candidates choose up to 5 tests from 37 (13 languages, 23 domain subjects and the General Aptitude Test). This mock combines two of those tests, the General Test and English, into a 120-minute, 100-question paper, and each section can also be run on its own in 60 minutes. Domain subjects follow the Class 12 NCERT syllabus and are not covered here. The question bank holds 60 original questions (30 per section). Scores are normalised percentiles per test.

trendAnalysis.summary: CUET UG 2024 was held in hybrid mode (pen-and-paper and CBT) with optional questions. From 2025 NTA reverted to CBT only, made all 50 questions compulsory with 60 minutes per test, and cut the maximum number of tests to 5, and 2026 continued this format. The General Test is easy to moderate: quantitative questions stay at about Class 8–10 level (percentages, ratio, averages, SI/CI, speed), and logical reasoning (series, coding, blood relations, directions, seating, syllogisms) has grown to roughly a third of the paper. GK has shifted towards static polity, history, geography and science, plus space and national schemes for current affairs. The English test is dominated by 2–3 reading passages (factual, narrative and literary), with the rest covering vocabulary, error spotting, voice and narration, idioms and sentence rearrangement. Time pressure rather than difficulty is the main challenge.

resources.notes: During the answer-key challenge window, NTA publishes the shift-wise question papers with provisional keys and each candidate's recorded responses on cuet.nta.nic.in. Final keys accompany the result. NTA does not keep a permanent public archive, so most full papers in circulation are memory-based or coaching reconstructions. The official syllabus PDFs for all 37 tests are on cuet.nta.nic.in.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability. Article 14 guarantees equality before law, Article 21 life and personal liberty, and Article 32 constitutional remedies.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following Indian states?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. It does not pass through Bihar.

questions.question: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten served as Governor-General from August 1947 to June 1948. C. Rajagopalachari was the first (and only) Indian Governor-General.

questions.question: Which gas makes up the largest share of the Earth's atmosphere by volume?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere, oxygen about 21% and argon about 0.93%.

questions.question: The Battle of Plassey was fought in:
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey took place in 1757. Buxar was fought in 1764 and the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761.

questions.question: India celebrates 23 August as 'National Space Day' because on that date in 2023:
options: Chandrayaan-3's lander touched down near the Moon's south pole
Gaganyaan's first crewed mission was launched
Aditya-L1 was launched towards the Sun
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander soft-landed near the lunar south pole on 23 Aug 2023. Aditya-L1 was launched on 2 Sep 2023, and Mangalyaan reached Mars orbit in 2014.

questions.question: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India established?
questions.explanation: The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934. It was nationalised in 1949, and 14 commercial banks were nationalised in 1969.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: Mercury, Venus, Moon, Mars
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets. The Moon is a natural satellite of the Earth.

questions.question: When the words Bridge, Brick, Bright, Bride and Brief are arranged in dictionary order, which word comes third?
questions.explanation: The dictionary order is Brick, Bride, Bridge, Brief, Bright, so the third word is Bridge.

questions.question: 1 January 2025 was a Wednesday. What day of the week was 1 January 2026?
questions.explanation: 2025 is not a leap year, so it has 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day. The day therefore moves forward by one, to Thursday.

questions.question: What is 25% of 480 plus 40% of 250?
questions.explanation: 25% of 480 = 120 and 40% of 250 = 100, so the total is 220.

questions.question: What is the simple interest on ₹8,000 at 6% per annum for 3 years?
The average of five numbers is 18. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining four becomes 16. What is the number that was removed?
questions.explanation: Total of five = 90 and total of four = 64, so the removed number is 90 − 64 = 26.

questions.question: A train 240 m long passes a pole in 12 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
An article bought for ₹600 is sold for ₹690. What is the profit percentage?
If A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 6 : 5, what is A : B : C?
If x + 1/x = 4, what is the value of x² + 1/x²?
The circumference of a circle is 44 cm. What is its area? (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: 2πr = 44 gives r = 7 cm, so the area is (22/7) × 49 = 154 cm².

questions.question: What is the mode of the data 3, 5, 7, 5, 9, 5, 7?
questions.explanation: 5 occurs three times, more often than any other value.

questions.question: How many cubes of edge 2 cm can be packed into a closed box with inner dimensions 10 cm × 8 cm × 6 cm?
What is the smallest number that must be added to 1000 to make it exactly divisible by 37?
questions.explanation: 37 × 27 = 999, so 1000 leaves a remainder of 1. Adding 37 − 1 = 36 gives 1036 = 37 × 28.

questions.question: Find the next number in the series: 4, 9, 19, 39, 79, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is (previous × 2) + 1, so 79 × 2 + 1 = 159.

questions.question: In a certain code, TEACHER is written as VGCEJGT. How is STUDENT written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves two places forward (T→V, E→G, …). So S→U, T→V, U→W, D→F, E→G, N→P, T→V, giving UVWFGPV.

questions.question: A is B's sister. C is B's mother. D is C's father. E is D's mother. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: A is a daughter of C (B's mother), and C is D's child. So A is D's granddaughter.

questions.question: Riya walks 10 m north, turns right and walks 6 m, then turns right again and walks 18 m. How far is she now from her starting point?
questions.explanation: She ends 6 m east and 18 − 10 = 8 m south of the start. Distance = √(6² + 8²) = 10 m.

questions.question:
Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red.
Conclusions: I. Some flowers are roses. II. Some roses are red.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: 'All roses are flowers' implies that some flowers are roses, so I follows. The red flowers need not include any roses, so II does not follow.

questions.question: In a row of 40 students, Ravi is 12th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?
questions.explanation: Position from the right = 40 − 12 + 1 = 29.

questions.question: Five friends P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. S sits in the middle. Q sits immediately to the right of P. R sits at one of the ends and to the left of S. T is not at either end. Who sits at the extreme right end?
questions.explanation: Since S is 3rd and R is at an end to the left of S, R is 1st. P and Q must be adjacent (P then Q), so they take positions 4 and 5. T fills position 2. The order is R, T, S, P, Q, so Q is at the extreme right.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 121, 144, 169, 196, 210
questions.explanation: 121, 144, 169 and 196 are the perfect squares 11², 12², 13² and 14². 210 is not a perfect square.

questions.question: Choose the number that completes the analogy: 3 : 27 :: 5 : ?
questions.explanation: 27 = 3³, so the second number is the cube of the first: 5³ = 125.

"Microplastics – fragments smaller than five millimetres – have now been found from the summit of Everest to the floor of the Mariana Trench. Some are manufactured at that size, such as the microbeads once common in face scrubs; most, however, are the result of larger items breaking down under sunlight and waves. Because they are so small, they are easily swallowed by plankton and fish, and they can carry toxic chemicals that cling to their surfaces. Scientists are still debating how seriously they threaten human health, partly because measuring particles this tiny in blood or tissue is technically difficult. What is not in doubt is that their quantity is rising: global plastic production has roughly doubled in two decades, and only a small fraction is recycled. Many researchers therefore argue that the most effective remedy is not better clean-up technology but producing less plastic in the first place."

According to the passage, most microplastics come from:
options: Larger plastic items breaking down under sunlight and waves
Plastic manufactured at a very small size
questions.explanation: The passage says some are manufactured small, but 'most, however, are the result of larger items breaking down under sunlight and waves'.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"When Meera's grandfather retired from the railways, he did something no one expected: he bought an old harmonium and enrolled in a music class full of ten-year-olds. The children giggled at first when the white-haired man fumbled with the simplest scales. He laughed along with them. Every evening, while the rest of the family watched television, the slow, wheezing notes of 'Sa Re Ga Ma' drifted from his room. Meera, embarrassed, once asked him why he bothered at his age. 'For forty years,' he said, 'I made sure trains arrived on time. Now I want to arrive somewhere myself.' Two winters later, at the colony's annual function, he played a full raga without a single mistake. Meera, sitting in the front row, was the first to stand up and clap."

What did Meera's grandfather do after retiring?
options: He started teaching music to children
He began organising the colony's annual function
He took a job at the railway station
He bought a harmonium and joined a music class
questions.explanation: The opening sentence says he bought an old harmonium and enrolled in a music class full of ten-year-olds.

questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to BENEVOLENT.
questions.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kindly.

questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to SCARCE.
questions.explanation: Scarce means in short supply, so its opposite is abundant. Rare, meagre and insufficient are near-synonyms of scarce.

questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to METICULOUS.
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, that is, painstaking.

questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to CANDID.
questions.explanation: Candid means frank and open, so its opposite is evasive.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling has a double 'c' and a double 'm': accommodation.

questions.question: Choose the correct word to fill the blank: "The new rules will ______ all employees from next month."
questions.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to influence. 'Effect' is usually a noun, or as a verb it means to bring about.

questions.topic: Grammar: Error Detection, Fill-ups, Voice & Narration
questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error: "Each of the boys / have finished / his homework / on time."
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so the verb must be 'has finished'.

questions.topic: Grammar: Error Detection, Fill-ups, Voice & Narration
questions.question: Fill in the blank: "She has been living in Pune ______ 2019."
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time in the perfect continuous tense. 'For' is used with a period of time.

questions.topic: Grammar: Error Detection, Fill-ups, Voice & Narration
questions.question: Choose the correct passive form of: "The committee will announce the results tomorrow."
options: The results would be announced by the committee tomorrow.
The results are announced by the committee tomorrow.
The results will be announced by the committee tomorrow.
The results will announced by the committee tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Simple future passive = will be + past participle, so 'will be announced'.

questions.topic: Grammar: Error Detection, Fill-ups, Voice & Narration
questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said, "I am tired."
options: He says that he was tired.
He said that I was tired.
He said that he was tired.
He said that he will be tired.
questions.explanation: With a past reporting verb, the present 'am' becomes 'was' and 'I' becomes 'he'.

questions.topic: Grammar: Error Detection, Fill-ups, Voice & Narration
questions.question: Fill in the blank: "He is ______ honest man."
questions.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (the 'h' is silent), so it takes 'an'.

questions.topic: Grammar: Error Detection, Fill-ups, Voice & Narration
questions.question: Fill in the blank: "He is senior ______ me by two years."
questions.explanation: Latin-origin comparatives such as senior, junior, superior and inferior take 'to', not 'than'.

questions.topic: Grammar: Error Detection, Fill-ups, Voice & Narration
questions.question: Fill in the blank: "If I ______ you, I would apologise at once."
questions.explanation: Hypothetical (second) conditionals use the subjunctive 'were' for all persons: 'If I were you…'.

questions.question:
Arrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: the old library
Q: was finally reopened
R: after years of renovation
S: in the town centre
questions.explanation: 'The old library (P) in the town centre (S) was finally reopened (Q) after years of renovation (R).'

questions.question:
The first sentence is given. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph.
1. Ravi woke up an hour late.
P: He ran all the way to the station.
Q: But the train had already left.
R: Skipping breakfast, he grabbed his bag.
S: Disappointed, he waited an hour for the next one.
questions.explanation: He grabs his bag (R), runs to the station (P), finds the train gone (Q), and waits for the next one (S).

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom 'to burn the midnight oil'.
options: To cook food late at night
To work or study late into the night
questions.explanation: 'Burning the midnight oil' means staying up late working or studying.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the phrase 'a blessing in disguise'.
options: Something that seems bad at first but turns out to be good
A person who pretends to be religious
A reward that comes too late
questions.explanation: A blessing in disguise is an apparent misfortune that later proves beneficial.

questions.question: Choose the one word for: 'a person who can speak many languages'.
questions.explanation: A polyglot knows many languages. A philanthropist helps others, a misanthrope dislikes people, and a bibliophile loves books.
